archetype: WU forced-draw punisher control: symmetric table draw made asymmetric three ways (Heliod's per-draw cost reduction, the hand-size upkeep punishers, and the Rhystic/Tithe tax layer), a two-effect pillow shell buying the waiting turns, eight counterspells defending them — and above all of it a four-card Aetherflux Reservoir storm kill that is rules-verified and rare: 0.7% of goldfish games assemble it, so the kill is the deck's ceiling and the upkeep clock is its median

role_assignment.default_role: Control, and specifically the control that owns the long game rather than the one waiting for a combo. Duke's inevitability test settles it: whoever loses a game that goes long enough must be the beatdown, and that is not you (strategy:whos-the-beatdown, strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). The punisher clock runs without tapping out — Iron Maiden deals hand size minus 4 and Ebony Owl Netsuke 4 at seven-plus cards, on each opponent's upkeep, before they get to spend the cards you gave them (verified stack 003) — while the counter suite holds the turns open (78.1% of goldfish games hold free-or-cheap interaction, 67.2% by turn six, mean turn 2.764). The hug-fort layer keeps the waiting political: Kwain and The Second Doctor hand out cards, and the Doctor's rider blanks the acceptor's next attack step (strategy:multiplayer.politics). Teferi, Hero of Dominaria is the posture made literal — his +1 draws and untaps two lands at the next end step, so the clock advances while the counter mana stays up.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: TWO pivots, and the common one is not the storm kill. The frequent pivot is threshold, not lethal: the turn a draw engine and a punisher are both on the battlefield (56.7% of games, 41.2% by turn six, mean turn 4.215), the deck stops accumulating and starts charging — every card you donate from that turn is damage on three upkeeps, and holding the engine back after the punisher lands is a free draw step for the table (strategy:pivot-point). The rare pivot is the storm arithmetic: commit only on the turn you can deploy Hullbreaker Horror, a cheap rock and Aetherflux Reservoir in one main phase, ideally behind Grand Abolisher, because stack 006 is honest that every loop cast and every 50-damage activation opens a fully open priority window and the engine protects none of them. Count the table's untapped mana first — assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window) — and hold the counterspell FOR the commit turn, not after it (strategy:pivot-point). Because the kill assembles in 0.7% of games, treat it as opportunism laid on top of the median plan, never as the thing you are waiting for (strategy:critical-mass.storm-math).

engines.piece: Howling Mine / Font of Mythos / Temple Bell / Dictate of Kruphix / Kami of the Crescent Moon / Folio of Fancies / Forced Fruition / Kwain, Itinerant Meddler / The Second Doctor / Jace Beleren + Iron Maiden / Ebony Owl Netsuke / Viseling / Psychosis Crawler / Sphinx's Tutelage / Scrawling Crawler
engines.engine: THE MEDIAN ENGINE, and the one the deck actually wins with. Ten cards force the table to draw; six charge for the resulting hand. It is a two-piece critical-mass machine — inert below the threshold, a table-wide clock past it (strategy:critical-mass): Iron Maiden and Viseling deal hand size minus 4 and Ebony Owl Netsuke deals 4 at seven or more cards, on each opponent's upkeep, so the charge lands before the cards get spent (verified stack 003). Two in-deck effects remove the cleanup brake outright: The Second Doctor and Folio of Fancies each read 'Players have no maximum hand size', so opponents never discard down to seven and the Maiden's X is uncapped. The measured shape is a gap, not a failure: a draw engine is drawn in 85.2% of games (75.4% by turn six), a punisher in 67.2% (55.9%), and BOTH in 56.7% (41.2% by turn six, mean turn 4.215) — the pair is a strict subset of the engine, so a real band of games reaches turn six holding donation with nothing to charge for it. Redundancy is the purchase here, not tutoring: ten cards is a 54% opener and six is 36% (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors).

engines.piece: Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring or Arcane Signet + Aetherflux Reservoir
engines.engine: THE VERIFIED KILL, AND THE RAREST THING THIS DECK DOES — both facts at once. Stack 006 walks a complete three-opponent kill in one main phase with an exact ledger: the mana-neutral alternating-bounce loop verified in stack 004 makes cast n net +n life off the Reservoir's 'you gain 1 life for each spell you've cast this turn', so k casts bank k(k+1)/2; from 32 life, 15 casts is the proven minimum funding three 'Pay 50 life' activations (14 fails at −13), ending at 2 life with the loop still running. The two-card form is REFUTED — stack 001 shows the cast trigger locks its target while the cast artifact is still a spell, so the pair alone does nothing — and stack 005 refutes the Displacer Kitten mana-positive extension, leaving a one-time +1 float. Now the measured half, which nothing had ever taken: the line assembles in 0.7% of goldfish games, 2.4% with the deck's one modelled unrestricted tutor, and 0.3% by turn six, mean turn 6.809. The arithmetic is not mysterious — it is an AND of three groups, two of which are single named cards. A named card is 7.1% of an opening seven and 10.1% by ten cards seen (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors), and Long-Term Plans is the ONLY card in the 99 that can search out Hullbreaker Horror; Enlightened Tutor reaches the Reservoir and both rocks but no creature. This is the ceiling build's signature: one spectacular finisher, and the game where it shows up is not the usual game (strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density).
engines.evidence: verified stacks 006 (aetherflux-storm-lethal), 004 (three-card engine, mana-neutral and unbounded), 005 (Kitten mana-positive REFUTED), 001 (two-card infinite REFUTED) — all checker.verdict == pass; goldfish_metrics.json target 'THE KILL (stacks 001/006)' assembled 0.7% / assisted 2.4% / by-t6 0.3% / mean turn 6.809; deck-audit engine block ranks it thinnest at 1 card, 7% in an opener; combo_details line Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring (bracket 1, mana_value_needed 0) contained per deck-facts

engines.piece: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse
engines.engine: the hinge that converts symmetry into asymmetry. The back face grants flash to everything you cast and reads 'Spells you cast cost {1} less to cast for each card your opponents have drawn this turn' — so the donation engines pay your mana bill and let you deploy at instant speed with counter mana still up. Every Howling Mine trigger is three cards drawn on their turns and a discount on yours; Forced Fruition turns one opposing spell into seven. This is virtual advantage in the strict sense: the opponents' own cards blank your costs without your drawing anything (strategy:card-advantage.virtual). The front face is a 4-mana enchantment creature whose ETB returns a nonGod enchantment from the graveyard, and transforming costs {3}{U/P} at sorcery speed — the discount is not free and not turn-four automatic. Goldfish has him cast on mean turn 4.133 (median 4), available in 90.2% of games by turn six.
engines.evidence: oracle text (both faces, cards.json); goldfish_metrics.json commander mean_cast_turn 4.133, median 4, cast_by_turn_6_rate 0.902; deck-facts colours note (front_face W, card union WU)

engines.piece: Enlightened Tutor + Mystical Tutor + Long-Term Plans
engines.engine: the consistency layer, and the honest ceiling on it. Per the tutors-as-copies frame, k tutors plus a card act like k+1 copies of every card in the deck (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors) — Enlightened Tutor at instant speed for {W} reaches every artifact and enchantment in the list (Aetherflux Reservoir, Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Thought Vessel, Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke, Forced Fruition, Rhystic Study, Smothering Tithe, Alhammarret's Archive, Propaganda), Mystical Tutor sets up Approach of the Second Sun, and Long-Term Plans is the only unrestricted search. The measured lift is real and small: goldfish's assisted figures raise the pair to 63.5%, wincon access to 68.0%, and the storm kill from 0.7% to 2.4%. Two honest costs the frame names: these tutor to the TOP or third from the top, not to hand, so the piece arrives a draw step or more later — a deck full of Howling Mines usually covers that gap — and Lowry's trade applies, the more tutors you play the fewer actual cards you get to play. Two of the ten Game Changers driving the bracket floor are in this package (Enlightened Tutor, Mystical Tutor); Long-Term Plans is not on the list.
engines.evidence: oracle text (Enlightened Tutor, Mystical Tutor, Long-Term Plans); goldfish_metrics.json *_assisted figures (kill 0.7%→2.4%, wincon access 61.2%→68.0%, pair 56.7%→63.5%) and the model assumption that only 'search your library for a card' tutors are modelled; bracket_report.json game_changers includes Enlightened Tutor and Mystical Tutor; deck-audit tutors axis 3 copies

engines.piece: Grand Abolisher + Fierce Guardianship / Force of Negation / Swan Song / An Offer You Can't Refuse / Counterspell / Dovin's Veto / Arcane Denial / Archmage's Charm
engines.engine: the protection layer the kill does not carry for itself. Stack 006 states plainly that each loop cast and each activation opens a priority window on an otherwise unprotected board; Grand Abolisher's 'During your turn, your opponents can't cast spells or activate abilities of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments' closes exactly those. Sequencing rule: Abolisher the turn before, or lead the commit turn with him. Failing that, the eight-card counter suite guards windows the expensive way — held protection ON the commit turn, which is what the pivot demands (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). Breadth is the suite's real virtue: Archmage's Charm's three modes (counter, draw two, steal a mana-value-1-or-less permanent) mean it is never a dead card, which is the flexible-answer discipline the interaction school prescribes (strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite) — and the answer-economy bar applies, hold the counter for the card that ends the game rather than the card that looks scary (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy). Note the taxonomy floor: the protection axis reads 1 copy (Teferi's Protection) against a 5-7 target because card_roles.json tags neither Grand Abolisher nor eight counterspells as protection.
engines.evidence: oracle text (Grand Abolisher, Archmage's Charm); verified stack 006 names the open windows and Grand Abolisher as the in-99 closer; goldfish_metrics.json 'Free or cheap interaction held' 78.1% / 67.2% by t6 / mean turn 2.764; deck-audit protection axis 1 copy vs 5-7 and interaction axis 14 copies (at target 12-15)

engines.piece: Teferi, Hero of Dominaria + Teferi, Temporal Pilgrim + Jace Beleren + Jace, Wielder of Mysteries
engines.engine: the sweep-surviving threat layer, four walkers deep — Duke's 'buy resilience instead of restraint' answer to sweeper exposure, made structural (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). None of them dies to Supreme Verdict, including your own, so you can reset a hostile board while your threats keep ticking. Teferi, Hero of Dominaria is the centrepiece: +1 draws and untaps two lands at the next end step (a clock that advances behind open counter mana), −3 is repeatable tuck removal that also answers a lock piece, −8 exiles a permanent on every draw in a deck built on drawing. Temporal Pilgrim self-charges off every draw and his −2 makes a Spirit that grows on every draw; Beleren's +2 is a table draw that feeds both the punisher math and Heliod's discount; Wielder of Mysteries +1 draws while a static threatens the empty-library win. In a format where you should assume the wrath arrives, deploying in waves behind permanents the wrath cannot see is the cheapest resilience available.
engines.evidence: oracle text (all four walkers, Supreme Verdict); deck-audit sweepers axis 1 copy (Supreme Verdict) and card-advantage axis 22 copies (target >= 10), all four walkers counted in it

engines.piece: Approach of the Second Sun + Mystical Tutor
engines.engine: Plan B, and the one that closes from a board the storm kill cannot use. First Approach resolves seventh from the top and gains 7 life; Mystical Tutor sets the redraw; the second cast wins during resolution. Stack 002 walks the interaction window on that second cast and finds it survivable behind held countermagic — Heliod's flash grant lets you cast it with mana up. Eisenherz's rule is exactly this shape: two primary combos, a Plan A and a Plan B, never more than two unconnected ones (strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density). Its access is far better than the storm kill's: wincon access sits at 61.2% of games (50.5% by turn six, mean turn 3.083). Note the seam — Enlightened Tutor cannot fetch a sorcery, so Mystical Tutor and Long-Term Plans are Approach's only searches.

engines.piece: Kwain, Itinerant Meddler + The Second Doctor + Propaganda + Alhammarret's Archive
engines.engine: the hug-fort: the layer that buys the waiting turns and gets paid for them. Kwain taps to let each player draw and gain 1; The Second Doctor's end-step offer carries a rider that blanks the acceptor's next attack step against you; Propaganda taxes every attacker {2}. Political cards are engineered dilemmas — every possible answer profits you, which is the exact standard the politics school sets (strategy:multiplayer.politics): decline and you keep the tempo, accept and you feed the Maiden. Alhammarret's Archive is the asymmetry hinge under all of it — your draws and life gain double while nobody else's does — and one pillow effect blanks attack plans from three players at once, virtual advantage tripled (strategy:card-advantage.virtual). The deflection budget is the thing to watch: this reads as the harmless donation deck exactly until the punishers land, and experienced tables discount 'I haven't done anything' from a player tracking draw engines (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection).
engines.evidence: oracle text (Kwain, The Second Doctor, Propaganda, Alhammarret's Archive); goldfish_metrics.json 'Table draw engine drawn' 85.2% / 75.4% by t6 / mean turn 2.507 (Kwain and The Second Doctor are members of that component)

engines.piece: Rhystic Study + Mystic Remora + Consecrated Sphinx + Smothering Tithe + Teferi's Ageless Insight + Faerie Mastermind
engines.engine: the asymmetric tax layer riding the turbulence the donation engines create. While the punishers charge for the table's hands, these convert the table's activity into your cards and treasure — and they scale with exactly the thing this deck manufactures. Two of them are draw doublers stacking with Alhammarret's Archive (Teferi's Ageless Insight), and Smothering Tithe is a mana source the audit counts among the 39. This is where inevitability actually lives: superior late-game card quality plus more answers than the table has threats is Duke's definition, and the audit's card-advantage axis reads 22 copies against a floor of 10 (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). Assembled with Heliod down in 71.0% of games, 54.0% by turn six.
engines.evidence: oracle text; goldfish_metrics.json 'Heliod down with an asymmetric card engine' 71.0% / 54.0% by t6 / mean turn 5.070; deck-audit card-advantage axis 22 copies vs target >= 10; mana_analysis.json counts Smothering Tithe among the nonland sources

engines.piece: Braingeyser / Stroke of Genius / Prosperity / Skyscribing / Mathemagics / Mikokoro, Center of the Sea + Psychosis Crawler + Sphinx's Tutelage
engines.engine: the burst half of the donation plan: six X-effects that fill every hand at once instead of a card a turn, turning the punishers on in a single shot rather than over three upkeeps. Mathemagics draws 2^X, Prosperity and Skyscribing draw X for each player, Braingeyser and Stroke of Genius can point at anyone, and Mikokoro is a land that does it every turn. The payoffs read off YOUR draws too: Psychosis Crawler drains each opponent 1 per card you draw and is as big as your hand, Sphinx's Tutelage mills two per draw and repeats on a colour match — and Alhammarret's Archive and Teferi's Ageless Insight each double every draw except the first in your draw step, so the burst turns are exactly where the doublers pay. Storm-math's ceiling/median split applies inside this layer as well: the giant Prosperity is the ceiling, the Howling Mine on turn two is the median, and you pace for the median (strategy:critical-mass.storm-math).
engines.evidence: oracle text (Mathemagics, Prosperity, Skyscribing, Braingeyser, Stroke of Genius, Mikokoro, Psychosis Crawler, Sphinx's Tutelage, Alhammarret's Archive, Teferi's Ageless Insight); deck-facts roles histogram draw:burst 6, draw:engine 12, draw:wheel 7; deck-audit threat-density axis counts Psychosis Crawler and Scrawling Crawler among the four wincon copies

engines.piece: Displacer Kitten + Loran of the Third Path + Torrential Gearhulk + Metallurgic Summonings
engines.engine: the value spine that converts a permission posture into board and answers. Displacer Kitten blinks a permanent on every noncreature cast — Sol Ring returns untapped, Loran re-triggers its 'destroy up to one target artifact or enchantment', Mystic Remora comes back a new object. Its degenerate extension is REFUTED (stack 005: both triggers lock targets at announcement and the blinked permanent is a new object, so the loop is not made mana-positive), which is precisely why the Kitten's job here is value. Torrential Gearhulk flashes in and recasts an instant from the graveyard for free, and Metallurgic Summonings makes an X/X Construct on every instant or sorcery cast — both reward the draw-go turns this deck spends anyway, and both matter because the audit's threat-density reads only 4 wincon copies against 15 creatures. Loran doubles as breadth: the audit finds 4 permanent classes answered against a target of 5, with graveyard uncovered (strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite).

The doubled ledger, the earliest legal first activation, and whether the reduced window count changes the Abolisher requirement are all unwalked

No checker-passed walkthrough covers the Abolisher-closes-006 claim, so the deck's central protection rule is currently oracle reading rather than verified

candidate_missing_lines.title: No maximum hand size makes Iron Maiden's X uncapped

The Second Doctor and Folio of Fancies both read 'Players have no maximum hand size', which should delete the 514.1 discard entirely and let Forced Fruition's seven-card refills accumulate across turns — Iron Maiden's 'hand size minus 4' then grows without a ceiling. The interaction of a static hand-size modifier with the cleanup step, and the real per-upkeep damage curve it produces, is unverified

candidate_missing_lines.title: Sphinx's Tutelage as a mill kill under two draw doublers

Whether the doublers stack multiplicatively for the trigger count, how the repeat clause resolves as a loop, and what X actually decks an opponent are all unwalked — and this is a second alternate kill riding hardware already in the 99

The new-object and counter-reset walkthrough, and the timing of the blink relative to your upkeep trigger, are unverified — this is the Kitten's most repeatable job in a deck where the mana-positive line is already refuted

candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Tithe triggers once per opponent draw with a {2} opt-out; Forced Fruition turns every opponent spell into seven draws, so one opponent turn can present seven-plus pay-or-treasure decisions. candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Drannith's 'Your opponents can't cast spells from anywhere other than their hands' should stop command-zone recasts; sweep or exile the commander and the 903.9-family replacement puts it exactly where Drannith locks it out. Which zone-change replacements apply, and that casting rather than the zone change is what is blocked, needs a walkthrough before this is presented as a lock

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: In the control mirror someone has to be the beatdown (strategy:whos-the-beatdown), and the punishers advance during draw-go, so inevitability is yours (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). The sweeper layering is structural: four planeswalkers live through every Supreme Verdict including your own, which is resilience bought instead of restraint (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). Teferi, Hero of Dominaria is the mirror's best card — his +1 advances while the end-step untap keeps two lands open — and Archmage's Charm's draw-two mode means held interaction is never dead in a permission stalemate (strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite). Supreme Verdict is your uncounterable reset through their permission. The real exposure is artifact and enchantment mass removal, which takes the donation engines and the punishers in one card, and creature wraths that answer Hullbreaker Horror before he ever loops. Keep the kill pieces in hand until the commit turn (strategy:pivot-point) — and given the line assembles in 0.7% of games, plan to win the mirror on the upkeep clock and the Approach, not on the storm.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Taxes attack velocity math directly, and this deck's plan is many cheap spells per turn — so recount the hand under the tax, and accept that under an assembling lock you rarely own the long game and your role flips to beatdown, racing the lock's completion (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial). Heliod's per-draw discount is a partial rebate that the donation engines keep feeding, which is a genuine structural answer rather than a hope. Repeatable outs matter more than a single counterspell here: Teferi, Hero of Dominaria's −3 tucks a lock piece every other turn, Loran of the Third Path destroys an artifact or enchantment on entry and again on every Displacer Kitten blink, and Cyclonic Rift resets a board of taxes at instant speed. You are partly the denial player yourself — Drannith Magistrate shuts off every opponent cast that is not from hand. Name the piece that beats YOU rather than the scariest piece, and sequence to protect the answer (strategy:resource-hedging.playing-to-outs).
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: Propaganda's {2} attack tax and The Second Doctor's attack-blanking rider are virtual advantage tripled — one pillow effect blanks attack plans from three players at once, the cheapest available answer to roughly 120 life of aggression (strategy:card-advantage.virtual). Say the honest part out loud: that is TWO attack taxes, and the audit reads protection at 1 copy against a 5-7 target, so the shell leans on never-dead interaction rather than a redundant third tax. The punishers convert defence into a clock and push the aggressor's damage-per-card below lethal (strategy:life-as-resource.philosophy-of-fire). Commit little and let them overextend into Supreme Verdict (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). The trap is structural: your donation engines refuel the aggressor's hand, so sequence a punisher before or alongside the big draw engines rather than after (strategy:critical-mass). Life-total caveat: the Reservoir kill pays 50 life three times, and against a fast board the 32-life starting point stack 006 assumes may not be there.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: Hold the eight-card suite for the card that actually ends the game — the answer-economy bar is 'ends the game or ends my deck's function', not 'looks scary' (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy) — and the goldfish says you hold something free or cheap in 78.1% of games, 67.2% by turn six. Drannith Magistrate blanks commander and non-hand-zone lines before they start. Then the uncomfortable half: you are usually NOT the faster combo deck. Your kill assembles in 0.7% of games (2.4% with the modelled tutor) at a mean turn of 6.809, which is slower and rarer than most dedicated combo decks in a bracket-4 pod, so against combo you are the control player and should assign the role that way (strategy:whos-the-beatdown). Play to your outs by keeping decisions in front of them — Forced Fruition hands a storm pilot seven cards per spell, which is the one card in this deck that can hand an opponent their own win (strategy:resource-hedging.playing-to-outs), and expect the table to discount your quiet artifacts and hit you anyway (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection).

distribution_notes: 85 entries / 100 copies; 33 land copies across 18 land entries (count copies, not entries). Nonland curve 9 / 21 / 15 / 11 / 5 / 3 / 2 / 1 at mana values 1-8, modal mana value 2 — squarely on the template genre's shape (strategy:deckbuilding.ratios). The base is 14 Island, 3 Plains, eleven UW duals and five utility lands (Ancient Tomb, Eiganjo, Otawara, Mikokoro, Flooded Strand). Only TWO lands enter tapped unconditionally (Irrigated Farmland, Temple of Enlightenment) against Karsten's roughly-four cap; the other five are shocks or condition-gated, and the audit's taplands axis reads at target (strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources). Colour sources: U 26 lands lifting to 31 with rocks against a 36 target, W 15 lifting to 20 against 22 — 5 and 2 short, the deck's one genuinely under mana axis. On-curve probability is 74.2% U / 78.7% W off lands alone, 83.9% / 88.1% with rocks. Pips skew hard blue: 61 U pips over 40 cards against 16 W over 14. Archmage's Charm is the only triple-pip card and Karsten's table asks 37 sources for {C}{C}{C} — treat it as a turn-four spell cast off duals and Heliod's discount, not a turn-three promise. Land count itself is the axis that answers itself: 33 lands against a 37-39 template, but 39 mana SOURCES against Burgess's 31 + 2 colours + commander mana value 4 = 37 (strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base). Two audit axes are taxonomy floors rather than holes — protection reads 1 next to Grand Abolisher and eight counterspells, and sweepers reads 1 against a 5-7 target whose own cited quote caps wipes at 'one or two max'. Interaction-breadth is a real 4-of-5 with graveyard uncovered. Roles cover 85.9% of the list and the 12 untagged cards are the plan itself — Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke, Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Dictate of Kruphix, Propaganda among them — so the role histogram systematically undercounts what this deck does. Synergy has 53 edges falling inside the deck, a global top-10 shortlist and not a per-deck fit score. Goldfish (seed 42, 10k iterations, decklist sha 2d7f07f99348): keep-first-seven 73.8%, mean mulligans 0.329, land-drop hit 86.6% on turn three and 47.1% on turn six; commander mean turn 4.133 (90.2% by turn six); table draw engine 85.2% (75.4% by t6); punisher 67.2% (55.9%); the pair 56.7% (41.2%); Heliod plus an asymmetric engine 71.0% (54.0%); interaction held 78.1% (67.2%); wincon access 61.2% (50.5%); THE KILL 0.7% (0.3% by t6, 2.4% assisted, mean turn 6.809). Mulligan rule from that spread: enabler-heavy hands dig toward punishers, punisher-only hands are blanks until an engine exists, and you mulligan to enabler CLASSES, not named cards (strategy:mulligans.engine-hands). Bracket floor 4, Optimized, on ten Game Changers plus the two-card-infinite signal — the listed Hullbreaker + Sol Ring infinite is refuted by stack 001 while stack 006 verifies the four-card kill, so the floor-4 conversation stays honest either way (strategy:deckbuilding.power-level).
overall_assessment: This deck plays the long game and owns it, and the thing it is famous for is not the thing it does. The world-view is Duke's inevitability (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock): every symmetric draw is asymmetric three ways — Heliod's per-draw discount, the hand-size punishers charging on each opponent's upkeep, and the Rhystic/Tithe/Sphinx tax layer — while a two-effect pillow shell and eight counterspells buy the turns and the hug pieces make the buying political (strategy:multiplayer.politics). Twenty-two card-advantage copies against a floor of ten, a turn-three land drop at 86.6%, the commander available in 90.2% of games by turn six: it functions, and it does not run out of cards. The uncomfortable number is the one now measured. The Aetherflux Reservoir kill is genuinely verified — stack 006 walks the full three-opponent ledger, 15 casts from 32 life, and stacks 001, 004 and 005 fence off what does NOT work — and it assembles in 0.7% of games, 2.4% with the modelled tutor, 0.3% by turn six, mean turn 6.809. That is not a defect in the simulation; it is what an AND of three groups looks like when two of them are single named cards, and when the only search that can find Hullbreaker Horror is Long-Term Plans. Storm-math already names the correct posture: separate the ceiling from the median, pace for the median, hold the ceiling as opportunism (strategy:critical-mass.storm-math). So play it as the punisher clock with a storm kill on top, not as a storm deck with a clock underneath. The median win is Iron Maiden and Ebony Owl Netsuke charging three hands you filled, closed out by Approach of the Second Sun at 61.2% access or a walker that outlived the wrath; the kill is the game where the table also gave you the fourth piece. Threat-density says as much in its own terms — the ceiling build runs one spectacular finisher and loses when it is answered, the median runs cheap ones and closes from any board (strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density) — and this list is honestly the second thing wearing the first thing's reputation. The named tensions, none of them fatal: 31 blue sources against a 36 target with a triple-pip Charm on top, a punisher half that arrives after the donation half in a real band of games, no graveyard answer at all, and a kill whose every priority window is open unless Grand Abolisher arrives first. The pivot rule follows: charge the clock the turn a punisher joins an engine, and take the storm turn only when the fourth piece and the shield show up together (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window).
